layers.description: Daily ocean-colour chlorophyll-a from VIIRS on NOAA-20, rendered by NASA GIBS. A measure of algae biomass near the surface.

freshness.note: Daily satellite composites usually appear 1-3 days after observation. Current: observed within 4 days. Stale: 5-10 days. Historical: older.

tiles.date_selection: Newest date advertised by GetCapabilities was 2026-10-07. Chosen date is the most recent of up to 7 days whose 3 probe tiles over central California returned HTTP 200 palette PNGs with data in at least 2% of pixels.

caveats: Chlorophyll measures algae biomass. It does not measure toxins and does not predict where fish are.
Clouds and fog leave gaps; a gap means no observation, not low chlorophyll.

layers.title: Satellite chlorophyll-a, Sentinel-3 OLCI 300 m, latest clear view
layers.description: Most recent valid chlorophyll-a observation from the OLCI sensor on Sentinel-3A, with Sentinel-3B filling gaps at each pixel within 7 days, with the date of each pixel.

freshness.note: Satellite overpasses are published about 2 (OLCI) to 5 (VIIRS 750 m) days after observation. Current: newest observation within 3 days. Stale: 4-7 days. Historical: older. In a 'latest clear view' every pixel also carries its own date.

tiles.date_selection: Rendered by CoastWatch from the published value grid: one source cell per tile pixel (nearest), cells without a value transparent.

caveats: Latest clear view: each pixel shows its most recent valid observation within 7 days; neighbouring pixels can come from different days. Check the observation date in the readout.
Chlorophyll-a measures algae biomass near the surface. It does not measure toxins, does not identify Pseudo-nitzschia and does not predict where fish are.
Clouds and fog leave gaps. A gap means no observation, not low chlorophyll. Gaps are never filled.
Values very close to shore, in river plumes and in shallow water are less reliable (bottom reflectance, sediment, land adjacency).
